messages:
maya: Heads up — noticed a ~30-40% token/sec drop on the continuous-batcher fleet after last night's release. Queueing depth is spiking and batch sizes are smaller than usual. Suspecting scheduler window change + KV cache churn.

junaid: Which release tag? any CI alerts?

maya: release: v2026.3.17-hotfix (deployed 03/17 23:40 UTC). Perf alert fired ~00:10 UTC. CI perf job also failed earlier this morning.

perf-bot: [ALERT] perf/continuous-batcher/tokenrate decreased 33% vs baseline on commit 9f3a2d. See: https://ci.redwood/bench/9f3a2d

maya: Pasted a short profiler excerpt from prod (aggregated across 6 machines):
```
token/sec: baseline=2300 -> now=1500
avg_batch_size: baseline=16.2 -> now=9.7
queue_latency_p95: baseline=35ms -> now=210ms
kv_cache_hit: baseline=0.88 -> now=0.62
kernel_choice: small-kernel favored (90%) vs expected mixed
scheduler.window_ms: 18 -> 60 (changed)
```

liam: who changed scheduler.window_ms? that seems huge.

junaid: I remember a PR that increased window to reduce tiny batches under tail workloads. Might have been #4128.

maya: I started a local bisect to confirm. Quick summary: reverting scheduler backoff in 9f3a2d/PR #4128 makes token/sec and batch sizes go back to baseline in canary.

maya: Repro command I used (canary):
```
kubectl exec -it cb-03 -- /bin/bash -c \"curl -s localhost:9100/metrics | grep continuous_batcher\"
# then compare token_rate and avg_batch_size over 5m windows
```

liam: If bisect points to #4128, that's a rollout blocker. We should hold and revert in prod ASAP.

deploy-bot: Rollout paused for v2026.3.17-hotfix due to alert: tokenrate-regression.

maya: Filed PR to revert the scheduler window bump: revert/4128 (patch attached). Also adding a quick KV hit-rate histogram probe to see whether the increased window caused more frequent KV evictions under our LRU heuristics.

junaid: Good. Can you also add an experiment to try alternative change: keep window small but add a gentle `idle_backoff_ms=8` so we don't thrash? Want to avoid oscillation.

maya: Yeah I'll add both: revert to previous window_ms=18, add idle_backoff_ms=8 and run perf-suite + canary.

sre-oncall: Please post when deployment is ready. We had a few downstream customer alerts for degraded chat experiences. Holding user-facing rollback if needed.

maya: Will coordinate. Quick note: KV cache hit drop looks like a secondary effect — with smaller batches we issue more requests, causing more active keys and pushing eviction. Fixing scheduler reduces request-per-second and restores hit-rate in canary.

liam: Sounds like root cause chain: scheduler window increase -> unexpected kernel selection skew (small-kernel bias) -> lower batch coalescing -> higher QPS -> KV churn -> more latency.

maya: Exactly. I'll push the revert and a canary monitor dashboard with these probes: `avg_batch_size`, `token/sec`, `kv_cache_hit`, `queue_latency_p95`, `kernel_choice_ratio`.

deploy-bot: Revert PR merged (revert/4128) by maya. Canary rollout started.

maya: Canary steady for 20m, token/sec back to ~2200 and p95 queue latency down to ~40ms. Monitoring for 1h before full rollout. :thumbsup:

liam: Nice work. After full rollout let's run a controlled experiment to quantify the tradeoffs of a slightly larger window with improved KV eviction policy. We should avoid repeated reverts.

maya: Agreed — will follow up with an RFC that includes microbenchmarks and a KV eviction sim.

sre-oncall: Thanks team — keeping this thread for postmortem notes.

maya: Adding a short root-cause blurb for the postmortem: "Regression introduced by scheduler.window_ms increase in PR #4128 which caused batching to fragment and indirectly reduced KV cache efficiency, producing token/sec regression and higher queue latency. Reverted the change and rolled back. Next steps: RFC for coordinated scheduler + KV eviction changes, defensive perf tests in CI for token/sec."
